verdicts.reason: The claim holds. E-6-2 has no in-edge, and tests/data.test.mjs 'every visa can be reached from "no visa yet"' lists it as lost. The 2026 manual extracts in data/visadocs.yaml show the status is in use and that its only way in is the shared E-6 CCVI from abroad, which includes the 공연법 performance case with a 영상물등급위원회 공연추천서; E-6-2 has no change list. Adding `- E-6-2` to NONE alone moves the failure to test 9 ('a move from abroad goes to a visa an embassy issues'), because visadocs has no E-6-2 abroad list. I checked on a scratch copy that the alias below makes both tests pass with no new failures. I could not reach the manual online: the WebFetch DNS lookups failed and the search budget was used up.
verdicts.correctedFix:
# data/visamap.yaml, NONE.next, right after `- E-6-1`:
    - E-6-2
# data/visadocs.yaml: give E-6-2 the shared E-6 CCVI list
  E-6-1:
    ...
    abroad: &e6abroad        # was `abroad:`
  ...
  E-6-2:
    abroad: *e6abroad
    extend: *id014
# (optional: narrow E-6-2 to the 'Performances under the Public Performance Act' variant only)

verdicts.reason: E-9 has no way to continue on E-9. The 3y + 1y10m ceiling is confirmed by the 2026 E-9 extension list in visadocs ('입국 후 3년 만료 재고용에 따른 최대 1년 10개월 추가 연장'). The statute (외국인고용법 제18조의4) could not be re-fetched: there is no network, and a no-departure 장기근속 reform may have changed it. The proposed self-move E-9 -> E-9 breaks the repo's data test 'every move goes to a known visa, once, and never to itself'. It also does not help the people it is for: the simulator shows the move BLOCKED[ageOnly] for any E-9 holder over 39, because the target's `age: [18, 39]` cannot be lifted per move. Put it in E-9's `how` text instead. A selectable move would need the test relaxed and the age cap moved to the entry moves (E-9 `age: [18]` plus `needs: {ageUnder: 40}` on the NONE, B-1, B-2, C-3-1, C-3-4, C-3-9, C-4, D-3 and E-8 moves into E-9); the simulator showed this works.
verdicts.correctedFix:
# data/visamap.yaml E-9 `how`: append one sentence (en below; ru, uz, uz-cyrl must be translated):
  en: '... citizens of N partner countries. Re-entry special case: if you finish 4 years 10 months without changing workplace (or only for the allowed reasons) and your employer applies before you leave, you can return once on a new E-9 one month after leaving, for up to another 4 years 10 months.'
# Do NOT add `{to: E-9, ...}` to E-9.next unless tests/data.test.mjs 'never to itself' is relaxed AND the 18-39 cap is moved from the E-9 node (age: [18]) to the entry moves as needs: {ageUnder: 40}.

verdicts.reason: In the repo, E-9 has `{to: D-2-2, abroad: true}` and E-10 does not, although its other next moves match E-9's. The D-2 change rule bars E-9 and E-10 alike from an in-Korea change, so the consulate route is the right way to model it. That matches the file's rule that abroad edges hang off statuses barred from changing in Korea. D-2-2 has an `abroad` list, and on a scratch copy the edge adds no test failures; the simulator shows it OPEN for an E-10 holder with edu 1. The restriction text comes from an earlier manual edition, quoted by a previous verifier; I could not re-fetch it.

verdicts.reason: E-6-2.next is only [F-6-1, F-2-3], while E-6-1 and E-6-3 offer D-2-2/3/4 as in-Korea changes. The D-2 change rule bars only C-3-2, C-3-3, D-3, E-9, E-10 and G-1 (E-8 too, per the finding), not E-6 or E-6-2. The exclusions that do single out E-6-2 (E-7, D-10 points exemption, F-2-7/F-2-R) are already honoured by the data. D-2-2/3/4 all have change lists. On a scratch copy the edges add no failures to test 8. The simulator shows D-2-2/D-2-3 OPEN and D-2-4 blocked on edu for an E-6-2 holder with a bachelor's. E-6-1's existing note already has all four languages, so no translation is needed.
verdicts.correctedFix:

verdicts.reason: I could not reach the cited easylaw page or the statute. The repo's 2026 manual extract handles injured E-9 workers through a fee-exempt E-9 extension (사업장변경신청기간 연장접수확인서 + 산재입증서류), which needs no change of status. That extract has no change list TO E-9 and none for any G-1 code. So both proposed in-Korea edges (E-9 -> G-1-x and G-1-x -> E-9) would fail the test 'a move inside Korea goes to a visa the manual lets you change to there'. The node code is also doubtful: from memory, KIS uses G-1-1 for 산재, not G-1-4. The new node would also need text in all four languages. Do not apply as written.

verdicts.reason: The contradiction is real. E-9's `how` says '17 partner countries' in all four languages, while the KZ note on the same visa says Kazakhstan was named an EPS partner in August 2026. The note was in the repo from its first commit; `countries: eps` correctly keeps 17 codes. I could not check the designation against a 고용노동부 primary source (no network); it rests on the two news reports cited plus the author's own note. The fix must change the number in all four `how` strings, not only the English one. No translation is needed, only the digit.
verdicts.correctedFix:
# data/visamap.yaml E-9 `how`: replace 17 with 18 in every language; keep `countries: eps` (17 codes) and the KZ note
  en: '... age 18–39, citizens of 18 partner countries.'
  ru: '... возраст 18–39, граждане 18 стран-партнёров.'
  uz: '... yosh 18–39, 18 hamkor davlat fuqarolari.'
  uz-cyrl: '... ёш 18–39, 18 ҳамкор давлат фуқаролари.'
